# Analyze validity of measuring running time vs cost
```{r}
perftest <- tibble(read.csv("../output/perftest_merged.csv"))

perf_df <- perftest %>%
  full_join(stats, by="graph")
```


Relationship between cost and time on some networks
```{r}
network_selection <- c( "coAuthorsDBLP.edges", "ca-citeseer.edges", "soc-twitter-follows.edges", "language.edges", "road-usroads.edges", "bio-grid-yeast.edges", "08blocks.edges")

perf_df %>%
  filter(graph %in% network_selection) %>%
  #filter(graph != "language.edges" | cost < 100) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=cost,y=time)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~graph, scale = "free")

perf_df %>%
  filter(graph %in% network_selection) %>%
  group_by(graph) %>%
  summarize(cor = cor(time, cost))
```

Let's look into 08blocks.edges a bit more closely!
```{r}
perf_df %>%
  filter(graph == "08blocks.edges") %>%
  filter(time < 0.001) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=cost,y=time)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.3) +
  labs(title = "only for time < 0.001")

perf_df %>%
  filter(graph == "08blocks.edges") %>%
  filter(time < 0.001) %>%
  summarise(correlation = cor(time, cost))
```


**Question:** what about the cost-time relationship over all networks?

```{r}
perfdf_avg <- perftest %>%
  group_by(graph) %>%
  summarise(dist=mean(dist),
            cost=mean(cost),
            time=mean(time),
           ) %>%
  full_join(stats, by="graph")

perfdf_avg %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=time,y=cost)) +
  geom_point()

print("Correlation across networks between average cost and average time:")
print(cor(perfdf_avg$time, perfdf_avg$cost))

corr_df <- perftest %>%
  group_by(graph) %>%
  summarize(correlation = cor(time, cost))

print("Correlation per network, summary:")
corr_df %>% select(correlation) %>% summary

corr_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = correlation)) +
  geom_density()

corr_df %>%
  left_join(stats)%>%
  ggplot(aes(x=n,y=correlation)) +
  geom_hex() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation coefficient between time and cost per network",
    x = "n",
    y = "Correlation coefficient between time and cost"
  )
```

# How good is the exponent estimation?

```{r}
fit_power_law_from_plot <- function(plot_obj) {
  # Extract the original data from the plot object
  plot_data <- plot_obj$data

  # Extract the variables from the aes mapping (x, y, color)
  mapping <- plot_obj$mapping
  x_var <- as_label(mapping$x)
  y_var <- as_label(mapping$y)
  color_var <- as_label(mapping$colour)

  # Use ggplot_build to get the color assignments
  plot_build <- ggplot_build(plot_obj)
  plot_colors <- unique(plot_build$data[[1]]$colour)  # Extract colors from the second layer (geom_point layer)

  # Ensure that the length of the colors matches the groups
  unique_groups <- unique(plot_data[[color_var]])

  if (length(plot_colors) != length(unique_groups)) {
    print(unique_groups)
    print(plot_colors)
    stop("Number of colors doesn't match the number of unique groups. Something went wrong.")
  }

  # Prepare a list to store the fitted lines
  fitted_lines <- list()

  for (i in seq_along(unique_groups)) {
    group <- unique_groups[i]

    # Filter data for the current group
    group_data <- plot_data %>%
      filter(.data[[color_var]] == group)

    # Fit the power-law model on log-transformed data
    fit <- lm(log10(group_data[[y_var]]) ~ log10(group_data[[x_var]]))

    # Extract coefficients
    coefficients <- coef(fit)
    intercept <- 10^coefficients[1]  # Back-transform intercept to original scale
    slope <- coefficients[2]         # Slope (exponent)

    # Print the coefficients and suspected power-law function
    print(paste("Group:", group))
    print(paste("Coefficient a:", intercept))
    print(paste("Exponent b:", slope))
    equation <- paste0("y = ", round(intercept, 3), " * x^", round(slope, 3))
    print(paste("The suspected function for", group, "is:", equation))

    # Create a fitted line using the extracted color for this group
    group_color <- plot_colors[i]
    fitted_lines[[i]] <- geom_abline(intercept = log10(intercept), slope = slope, color = group_color, linetype = "dashed")
  }

  # Return the fitted lines as a list of geom_abline layers
  return(fitted_lines)
}

```


```{r}

meancost_df <- perf_df %>%
  filter(girg_scale) %>%
  left_join(girg_stats) %>%
  mutate(ple = as.factor(ple)) %>%
  group_by(n_gen, ple, temp, sample) %>%
  summarise(
    cost = mean(cost)
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    cost = mean(cost)
  ) %>%
  filter(temp==0.1) %>%
  ungroup()

plot<-meancost_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n_gen, y = cost, color = ple)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() + annotation_logticks()

lines <- fit_power_law_from_plot(plot)

plot+lines

meancost_df %>%
  mutate(
    est_exp = log(cost) / log(5*n_gen),
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n_gen, y = est_exp, color = ple)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10() + annotation_logticks() +
  geom_smooth(method='lm')



```
